title: Credit-billed pinned products: mint refusals and per-run trade-offs
answers: Why didn't a sandbox run get an AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN?
Why does a run with an open-weight model stay on the Python gateway?
What happens when a team is out of AI credits for a gateway-minted run?
body:
For products in `AI_CREDITS_BILLED_PRODUCTS` (posthog_ai, slack_app, workflows) the mint is refused when the team is out of AI credits, and for products in `PRODUCT_ALLOWED_MODELS` it is refused with `model_outside_pin` for off-pin models (e.g. open-weight zai-org/kimi). Enforced via `mint_refusal` in products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/ai_gateway_token.py; `ai_gateway_env_vars` then omits `AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and the run falls back to the Python gateway.
Known trade-offs: credits are checked once at run start (not mid-run), and a pinned run cannot switch to an off-pin model mid-run.
posthog_ai origin stays API-settable (task tracker creates tasks via the public API), so eligibility relies on these refusals and the team billing rather than origin reservation.
applies: Products minting Go gateway tokens that bill AI credits or carry a model pin.
